FM05.reasoning: The dataset is a time series (predicting future bike demand), but the agent uses shuffled K-Fold cross-validation instead of a time-based split, introducing look-ahead bias.

FM12.reasoning: The agent combines models using hardcoded, arbitrary weights without tuning the blend ratio via cross-validation or stacking.

other_failure_modes.name: Unused categorical features declaration
other_failure_modes.description: The agent defines a list of categorical features for tree-based models but fails to pass this list to the models during training, causing the models to treat categorical features (e.g., season, weather) suboptimally as continuous numerical features.

other_failure_modes.name: Incorrect submission format
other_failure_modes.description: The agent creates a submission file with an auto-generated sequential ID column instead of using the original identifiers required by the task (e.g., 'datetime'). This will cause the submission to fail automated evaluation.

other_failure_modes.name: No validation score computed
other_failure_modes.description: Although the agent sets up a cross-validation split and uses validation sets for early stopping, it never computes or reports the validation metric on the hold-out folds, leaving the user with no offline estimate of model performance.
other_failure_modes.evidence: The cross validation loop finishes without generating predictions on X_va to compute an overall RMSE or RMSLE score.

summary: The provided solution correctly frames the RMSLE optimization by log-transforming the target and extracting basic datetime features. However, it critically fails by using a shuffled K-Fold split instead of a time-based split, which introduces look-ahead bias in a time-series problem. Furthermore, it defines but ignores categorical features, fails to compute any validation score during cross-validation, and produces an invalid submission format by using a sequential ID instead of the required 'datetime' column.
